name: Cooker
description: Open-source, self-hosted CI/CD tool with a drag-drop graph pipeline editor. Single Go binary. Builds OCI images without docker.sock (Kaniko, BuildKit, Buildah), deploys to Kubernetes, AWS ECS, Google Cloud Run, Fly.io, and Render. MIT-licensed, no SaaS, no agents.
abstract: Cooker is a self-hosted CI/CD platform that gives developers a visual DAG editor for designing pipelines. Drag Build, Test, Push, Deploy, and Approval nodes onto a canvas, draw edges, and click Run. Built on Go and React. Ships as a single binary. MIT licence. Single-tenant today.
featureList: Visual drag-drop DAG pipeline editor powered by React Flow
OCI image builds via Kaniko (default, no docker.sock), BuildKit, and Buildah
Deploy targets: Kubernetes, AWS ECS/Fargate, Google Cloud Run, Fly.io, Render, SSH remote
Multi-environment promotion with RBAC-gated approval gates
Four-role RBAC: admin, operator, approver, viewer
Five pluggable secrets backends: Postgres AES-GCM, KeepSave, HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, GCP Secret Manager
Prometheus metrics and OpenTelemetry OTLP traces (opt-in)
Per-route audit log (on by default in production)
Helm OCI chart for production Kubernetes install
Multi-arch container image: amd64 + arm64, non-root UID 65532, cosign-signed
keywords: CI/CD, self-hosted, open-source, visual pipeline editor, DAG, Kubernetes, OCI, Docker, Kaniko, Go, single binary
